svg.title: Index arithmetic IS the tree
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing seven values drawn once as a binary tree and once as a flat array of seven boxes with indices zero to six, dotted lines connecting each tree node to its array slot, and the index arithmetic left equals 2i plus 1, right equals 2i plus 2, parent equals i minus 1 over 2 written beside it, with explicit parent and child pointer fields crossed out in red; a level-by-level accounting showing that half the nodes are leaves needing zero swaps while only the root needs log n, summing to linear work; a sift-down swapping down past the smaller child; and measured bars of 22.7 milliseconds for bottom-up heapify against 42.0 milliseconds for a million successive pushes.
svg.text: the array IS the tree. There are no pointers.
index arithmetic already told you where
everything is. Storing it again is waste.
why building it is O(n), not O(n log n)
half the nodes are leaves and do NO work. That one
sentence is the whole proof - and it is why
compare with BOTH, swap with the SMALLER
(swap with 9 instead, and the left side breaks)
1.85x - and it is not even close in cache misses
...week 27: HNSW's candidate queue is exactly this
